title: Two-center metric coordinates with smooth proximity features
coverage_gap: The exact twenty demonstrations contain ten LL and ten HH layouts, but no LH or HL. Separate world nut and peg x channels can therefore stand in for one another. The observed handle is not the ring center; treating the native object site as the insertion point would introduce an approximately 0.13 m offset.
reusable_regularity: Grasping depends on the hand-to-handle edge, while assembly alignment depends on the ring-to-peg edge. Supply these relations explicitly in world axes, with fixed physical units rather than narrow-support coordinate standard deviations. A second smooth signed proximity scale emphasizes centimeter errors without losing long-range edges. This is a deterministic 56-dimensional representation with no learned encoder, no explicit stage, and no auxiliary loss; the common U-Net learns the action sequence.
dependencies_preserved: The 0:3 world hand location, centered at [0,0.6,0] and scaled by 0.3 m, preserves robot workspace dependence rather than assuming global translation invariance.

Edges use 4:7 handle, 39:42 ring center, and 36:39 peg goal separately. World ring and goal positions can be reconstructed from the hand and these edges; heights relative to the world table are explicit.

Current and native-previous gripper, hand/handle increments, and both wxyz orientations converted to continuous rotation columns preserve contact and inertial cues. The two whole causal observations preserve measured ring motion.

No obstacle channels exist beyond the declared table/world and peg geometry. Absent object2 zero fields are omitted; no undeclared geometry is used. Fixed world axes preserve gravity and the native fixed gripper orientation.

evidence_refs.detail: assembly__N20__rep0, twenty exact support identities and hashes
LL/HH support, C and E definitions; handle site versus ring center; wxyz, world action4 and common raw42 semantics
cell_counts HH=10, LL=10; demo_00 through demo_03 ranges include low grasp height and high carried object height
obs rows 0-2: handle x 0.1078 versus ring x -0.0222; rows 26-29, 45-47, and 72-74 show grasp, lift and alignment geometry; actions 0-86 show the switches
Initial ring, offset handle, peg and table geometry
Gripper at the handle rather than ring center
Ring aligned at the upright peg

expected_failure_signature: If explicit edges do not eliminate the correlation shortcut, cross-cell runs should grasp successfully yet move the ring to the x associated with the nut rather than the actual peg. E may still fail at long lateral displacements unseen in support. A separate failure is premature descent or lift under four-step execution because no stage structure is imposed. These are predictions, not measured outcomes.

required_runtime_fields.input: context.raw_history [B,2,42] only; normalized causal_history is intentionally replaced with fixed metric scaling
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity encode/decode on all sixteen native actions: world_dx, world_dy, world_dz in native 0.01 m units, gripper unchanged. Only the public executor clips in world native action space and executes four actions.

support_fit: None; no fitted statistics or cached labels. Fixed scales are physical design constants, not estimates from other data. Common raw normalization remains host-owned.
change_summary: Initial executable design. Replaces raw coordinate conditioning by explicit two-center geometry and sign-invariant orientation; leaves action encoding, action epsilon loss, all masks, diffusion schedules and optimizer unchanged. No performance feedback used.
